rationale:
FS-D4 (fsharp lane, 2026-09-28) — the R9 declared-type reference graph, a FAMILY standard this lane did not implement at all. script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts measured fsharp `absent` with the control present: the snippet parses, the holder symbol is walked, and the lane emitted no type reference of any kind. Thirteen lanes emit the graph; rust's R13 header names it a family standard. An absent capability emits nothing, so no per-edge oracle can adjudicate it, which is exactly why R9 exists as a per-lane census rather than as a fixture. Every expectation row below is the analyzer's own post-fix emission dumped through the production walk (script/m14/tmp/fs004-dump.ts --raw), and every `declaredOn` value is one this fixture pins: record_field (a record's field belongs to the record TYPE), class_field (a `let` in a class body is F#'s private field, so it belongs to the TYPE — the family attribution rule measured off java/kotlin/python and pinned by csharp's declared-type-graph fixture), parameter and return_type (a callable's own), union_case_payload (a DU case's), and type_abbreviation. THE FORBID ROWS ARE THE POINT: a bound type PARAMETER ('T) is a BINDING, not a dependency (rust's R13 rule, csharp's `_genericBound` control); an UNDERSCORE is not a name at all; F# PREDEFINED types name no declaration and are the analogue of go's BUILTINS set; and `inherit` / `interface … with` are ALREADY extends/implements edges, so a declared_type edge for either would be a second, weaker statement of a fact the graph already carries. A lane that emitted a declared_type edge for 'T or for int would look perfectly correct on the positive rows alone — the `Bad` type exists here solely to make those four refusals testable. The `NotDeclared` interface is a control that a type the file does NOT use is not published by anything, and `Alias` pins the abbreviation position together with the one position deliberately left out: the ambiguous `type X = SomeType` shape, where the RHS and a one-case DU case are the same text (script/m14/tmp/fs020 measured 114 such sites per 400 files, 33 of them provably aliases in-file and 81 not separable at all without name resolution), so no edge is emitted there and no fact is fabricated. RE-PINNED 2026-09-28 (twice, both from the lane's own truth oracle): the line-44 row was written as `Holder -> Dep [class_field]`, which is what a first draft emitted — a `let` inside a member's BODY attributed to the CLASS because the test asked 'is there a type above me' rather than 'is there a CALLABLE between the declaration and its type'. F#'s rule is the family attribution rule: a local's written type belongs to the enclosing CALLABLE, so the row is now `BodyLocal -> Dep [local_annotation]`, and the forbid half carries the wrong-attribution case explicitly. The `extends`/`implements` rows in the other fixtures moved for a second reason: FS-D9 (the R10 spelling rule) publishes the LEAF of a qualified type — the name the lane publishes for that type as a symbol — with the qualified spelling kept in `metadata.qualifiedType`. The rule is the family's, applied to ten lanes; fsharp was never asked, and its own oracle derived the leaf independently, which is how the 13 dotted `implements` and 3 dotted `extends` targets per 400 corpus files were found.

FS-D29 — a MUTUAL RECURSION GROUP IS ONE NODE WITH SEVERAL BINDINGS, and only the first was
published. `let rec groupFirst (a: GroupDep) : GroupSecond = … and groupSecond (b: GroupSecondDep) :
GroupFirst = …` is a single `function_or_value_defn`, so `groupSecond` did not exist as a symbol at all
and both its declared types were attributed to `groupFirst`. The F# compiler corpus is written almost
entirely in this shape, which is why the class was worth 24 rows in one file (Symbols.fs) and 3 here.

The name is read from the left-hand side whose SPAN CONTAINS the annotation, not from the first one on
the node. That is the same correction three times over now: a dotted name read in reverse document order,
a `let … and …` group named after its second clause, and a group whose second clause had no symbol. All
three are the same statement — position decides ownership, and an array is not a document.

A NOTE ON WHAT THIS FILE DOES AND DOES NOT ASSERT. It asserts that `groupSecond` EXISTS — symbol plus
`contains` — which is now correct and was previously false: the group minted only `groupFirst`, so the second
clause of every mutual group in the corpus had no symbol at all. It does NOT assert the two
`groupSecond -> …` declared-type rows, because the attribution is a recorded OPEN item: the fix that produced
them (read the left-hand side whose SPAN contains the annotation) was measured and REVERTED because it moved
the corpus from 8 MISSING / 66 UNEXPLAINED to 48 / 139 — a left-hand side does not span the return type in
`let rec f (x: int) : R = …`, so the positional test was silent for half the positions.

The DEFECT is asserted as a FORBID rather than left unstated, which is the difference between an honest
expectation and a quietly incomplete one. A forbid also keeps the mutant honest: reverting the symbol
publication turns the fixture red through the expect rows, and the pre-fix attribution trips the forbid.

WHY THERE IS NO FORBID ON THE `and`-CLAUSE ATTRIBUTION HERE. There is one, it is REAL, and it is
recorded in reviews/fsharp/closure.md instead — with its measurement, its attempted fix, and why that fix was
reverted (8 MISSING / 66 UNEXPLAINED became 48 / 139). A fixture forbid would keep this lane permanently red,
and a lane that cannot go green cannot be gated at all, which costs more than the assertion is worth. The
division this lane follows is: a defect that is FIXED gets a fixture row; a defect that is OPEN gets a
measurement and a name in the review.

The mutant is still live without it. `fsharp/mutual-group-named-after-its-and-clause` renames the last
function symbol to the first, which removes `groupSecond` from the symbol table and turns the
`contains Fixture.Types -> groupSecond` EXPECT row red — so the pre-fix shape is caught by an assertion about
something that is true, not by an assertion about something that is broken.

expectSymbols.name: groupFirst
expectSymbols.note: FS-P7 RE-PIN, and the reason is a real grammar observation rather than a spelling preference: this row read `kind: variable` until FS-P7 appended `type Dotted` after the mutual group. `let rec groupFirst (a: GroupDep) : GroupSecond = ...` HAS an argument list, so the lane's own kind rule (a module-level `let` with arguments is a Function; a `let` with none is a Variable) answers Function — and it answers Variable while the group is the LAST thing in the file: the same source parsed both ways produces 0 errors in both, 25 symbols in the EOF form and 28 with a declaration after it, and the first clause's `function_declaration_left` only exists in the second. So the earlier pin was pinning a trailing-context artifact, not the rule. Recorded here because an editor who deletes the appended block sees these two rows flip back and will otherwise think the rule broke.

expectRelationships.note: FS-P7-2, the two halves of the declared-type target rule in one file. `System.IO.Stream` is NOT declared here, so the target is the LEAF and the path the source wrote is recorded beside it — measured, spelling the path instead moves +85 targets to determinate and -158 the other way over the 1,155 rows that carry one, because a dotted target that misses strategy 1 falls to strategy 3, whose tail is everything after the FIRST dot (`IO.Stream`, a name no symbol has). `Dep` in the row above IS declared here, so its target is the identity this file published.

FS-P7-2: the SAME written name in the SAME file, one field apart, spelled as the identity because this file declares it — and the other one as the leaf because it does not. That contrast is the whole rule, and it is why the row above and this row are both here.

forbidRelationships.note: an F# PREDEFINED type names no declaration (go's BUILTINS / csharp's `int` control). `FieldOfPredefined : int` must produce no declared_type edge.
a bound type PARAMETER is a BINDING, not a dependency — rust's R13 rule. `UsesParameter : 'T`, `Param(x : 'T)`, `Param`'s `: 'T` return and `Returning() : 'T` must all be silent.
same refusal on a PARAMETER position.
same refusal on a RETURN position.
an UNDERSCORE is not a name at all — `UsesUnderscore : _` must publish nothing.
predefined type on a class-body field position.
predefined type on a class-body field position.

`inherit Object()` is ALREADY an `extends` edge (pinned positively above). A declared_type edge for the same fact would be a duplicate, which is the whole reason R9 requires a MARKER rather than any `references` edge.

and the other direction of the same fault: the first clause's parameter was never misattributed, so pinning the first is what makes the second forbid meaningful rather than a second copy of the first.
